So as you've-- This is probably just rehashing what everybody else has said, but
sensitive species data are basically data about species that have features
that mean there are reasons for withholding the data from public view or modifying
the data before it is made public.
And we're tending to use the terminology of restricted access
species data within the task group now because of the word
"sensitive" tends to cause people to feel reticent about sharing their data
rather than about making it open, but in a way that protects
the sensitivities of the data.
And most of what the task group has been talking about is how we can go about
protecting the importance of this kind of sensitive data,
but still allow the data to be accessible in some form to
people who need to see it.
